🇲🇽 In the 1970s, Mexican actress Lyn May was approached by a woman who claimed she could enhance her beauty with a simple injection.

Trusting her, Lyn allowed the woman to inject her cheeks with what was supposed to be collagen.

It was actually a mix of cooking oil and baby oil.

At first the results looked fine. Then hard lumps began forming under her skin. Her face gradually changed shape and never returned to normal.

Lyn underwent multiple surgeries over the years trying to remove the oil, but each operation only added more scars. 

The damage was permanent.

The transformation left her so devastated that she later admitted she considered ending her life.

Decades on, doctors still have not been able to extract all of the oil from her face.

Muhammad Ali, 30, told Johnny Carson why champions go broke. At 38, he was still taking punches for $8M.

November 1972. The Tonight Show.
A ban had cost Ali over 3 years of his prime. The Frazier fight paid $2.5M.

Carson asks if he'll end up broke.
Beau Jack, a former champion, is "shining shoes somewhere down in Florida."

Ali blames the men around the fighters.

"He cannot watch his money. He cannot watch his accountants. He cannot watch his lawyers or his managers."
"Half of them are crooked and conniving."

The managers went to school for money. The fighter didn't.

"They always remember the name Joe Louis."

Louis made millions. He ended up owing the IRS over $1M and greeting tourists at Caesars Palace.

And Ali's own money?
"I have accountants and everybody checking everybody."

8 years later, he lost to Holmes.
Parkinson's followed in 1984.

In 2006, he sold 80% of his own name for $50M.

The money held. The body didn't.

"It won't be because I wasn't watching."
